validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within a Japanese-American cohort measuring serum lycopene before diagnosis with incident, tissue-confirmed prostate cancer as outcome; no lycopene-specific estimate is reported but the target exposure and outcome are present.

extraction.population: Japanese-American men in a cohort of 6860 examined from 1971 to 1975

cases.excerpt: After a surveillance period of more than 20 years, 142 tissue-confirmed incident cases of prostate cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: The odds ratio for the highest quartiles were 1.8 (95% confidence interval, 0.9-3.9) for beta-cryptoxanthin, 1.6 (0.8-3.5) for beta-carotene, 0.8 (0.4-1.5) for retinol, and 0.7 (0.3-1.5) for gamma-tocopherol, but none of the differences was statistically significant.

validated_results.title: Adult height and incidence of cancer in male physicians (United States).
validated_results.reason: The analysis examines adult height and cancer incidence, with beta-carotene appearing only incidentally as the trial's randomized treatment assignment used for adjustment, so no beta-carotene exposure estimate for prostate cancer is provided.

validated_results.title: Adipose fatty acids and cancers of the breast, prostate and colon: an ecological study. EURAMIC Study Group.
validated_results.reason: The prostate cancer finding is reported only for aggregated n-6 fatty acids in adipose tissue in an ecological correlation, with no linoleic acid-specific prostate cancer estimate separable from the fatty acid mixture.

validated_results.title: The in vitro effect of vitamin D3 analogue EB-1089 on a human prostate cancer cell line (PC-3).
validated_results.reason: This is an exclusively in vitro preclinical study of a vitamin D3 analogue on the PC-3 prostate cancer cell line with no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Vitamin D receptor: no evidence for allele-specific mRNA stability in cells which are heterozygous for the Taq I restriction enzyme polymorphism.
validated_results.reason: The study addresses vitamin D receptor allele-specific mRNA stability in cell lines and lymphocytes, providing no population-wide vitamin D exposure estimate for prostate cancer incidence.
